text: Multiplying both marginals by a>0 scales every coupling by a and its Lp objective by a^(1/p). The inverse scaling gives equality of the infima, consistent with [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s definition and [Mathlib’s Lp convention](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92). The hypotheses exclude zero and infinite scaling, where that bijection fails. At p=∞ the factor is one; at p=0 the totalized convention is preserved. The published [finite-measure attainment theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L1102) uses this exact normalization and rescaling identity.
Published consumer checks finite nonzero mass normalization/rescaling and a separate zero-mass case; no claim of a new numerical fixture.

The displayed plan leaves σ on the diagonal and moves τ to x₀. Its second marginal is exactly σ+τ(univ)δx₀, preserving mass even when τ is infinite. The zero-displacement part contributes nothing, so the objective is the stated Lp norm against τ alone. This is the admissible-plan bound in [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82). The [published Dirac identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L514) checks the probability case with σ=0. Joint measurability supports the restriction and pushforward argument; no p≥1 assumption is needed.
A probability law transported wholly to an atom has exactly its Lp distance-to-atom cost.

The same witness basepoint works after multiplying the measure by any finite nonnegative scalar: Lp membership is preserved under that change of measure. This agrees with [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s integral moment convention and includes p=∞ through [Mathlib’s seminorm definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92). Zero scaling is allowed here, unlike the distance-scaling equality, because only preservation is claimed. The hypothesis already supplies a basepoint, so the existential predicate is not silently asserted for an empty ground type. No finite-total-mass assumption is required.

Both measures can be tested at one basepoint by [published basepoint independence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L696). For 0<p<∞, the moment integral against μ+ν is the sum of two finite integrals, matching [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s moment definition. At p=∞ the larger of their essential bounds works; p=0 is handled separately by measurability. Thus the theorem retains the finite-measure and ordinary-pseudometric hypotheses needed to put the witnesses at a common point. It asserts moment closure under addition, not preservation of probability normalization.
Published common-basepoint equivalence supplies the correct finite-measure and measurability conditions.

For a coupling π, its coordinate marginals identify the Lp norms of distance-to-x₀ with those under μ₀ and ν. Triangle inequalities then show that displacement belongs to Lp exactly when ν has finite moment, provided μ₀ already does. This is the coupling estimate behind [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s finiteness proof. The [published anchor criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L798) consumes both implications. The first-marginal moment assumption is essential; no optimality or probability normalization is required for this fixed-plan equivalence.
Published finite-anchor equivalence uses both directions of coupling moment transfer.

A finite nonnegative sum bounds its selected summand. Because w(i)≠0 and q>0, infinite Wp(ν,μᵢ) would make that summand infinite. Symmetry and [the published finite-anchor criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L798) then transfer μᵢ’s p-moment to ν, agreeing with [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s moment geometry. The displayed `i∈s` prevents an empty-support argument, and zero weights cannot supply the anchor. Infinite weights are legitimate: finiteness then forces the selected distance to vanish. No normalization of the weights is claimed.
Published finite-anchor equivalence uses both directions of coupling moment transfer.

For 0<p<∞, taking the positive pth power of the plan bound turns its Lp norm into ∫d(x,y)^p dπ. The result is exactly [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s admissible-plan bound for Wp^p. Joint measurability justifies the norm/integral formula, and the two endpoint exclusions keep `p.toReal` positive. The [two-Dirac cost formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Cost/Basic.lean#L288) and [two-Dirac distance formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L487) are published controls with matching powers. No optimizer, probability measure, or triangle inequality is assumed.
Source-present Dirac cost calibration returns the cost evaluated at the pair of atoms.
Source-present Dirac distance calibration returns the ground distance for every nonzero exponent, including∞.

Both sides optimize over exactly the same couplings: the left raises their Lp-infimum to p, while the right minimizes the integral of d^p. Positive power and reciprocal power preserve order on [0,∞], proving the identity in [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s Definition 6.1. The [Dirac cost Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Cost/Basic.lean#L288) and [Dirac distance Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L487) agree. The signature correctly excludes p=0 and p=∞ and retains measurable ground distance. Empty coupling families and infinite values remain ∞ on both sides.
Source-present Dirac cost calibration returns the cost evaluated at the pair of atoms.
Source-present Dirac distance calibration returns the ground distance for every nonzero exponent, including∞.

`IsOptimalCoupling` includes both correct marginals and equality with the infimal integral cost. The [published cost identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L964) and injectivity of positive powers turn that equality into the displayed Lp-attainment condition. This matches the minimization problem in [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82). The [Dirac optimality Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Cost/Basic.lean#L364) passes. Infinite optimal values remain allowed; the theorem characterizes a supplied plan and does not assert that an optimizer exists or has finite displacement.
Source-present Dirac-source optimality control: the unique feasible plan is optimal, including infinite costs.

For the supplied optimal coupling, its integral is the primal optimum by definition. The [cost bridge](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L964) identifies that optimum with Wp^p, giving exactly the displayed equality. This is [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s finite-p convention. The [Dirac cost formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Cost/Basic.lean#L288) provides a native normalization check. Both sides may be infinite: the theorem does not infer integrability from optimality alone. The finite, nonzero exponent and measurability assumptions are retained.
Source-present Dirac cost calibration returns the cost evaluated at the pair of atoms.

Optimality makes this plan’s Lp objective equal to Wp; `hfin` then makes it finite, and measurable ground distance supplies the other part of `MemLp`. The [published attainment equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L993) verifies that exact step. This agrees with [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s moment interpretation. The explicit finite-distance hypothesis matters because an optimal plan can still have infinite cost. No separate marginal-moment assumptions are needed: two infinite-moment laws may have finite displacement from one another.
Published exact correspondence between integral-cost optimality and Lp-infimum attainment, with feasibility retained.

The right side is the pth root of the minimum integral cost, precisely [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s Definition 6.1. It follows from [the published power identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L964) by the positive reciprocal exponent. The [Dirac cost Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Cost/Basic.lean#L288) and [Dirac distance Check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L487) confirm that the root recovers ground distance. Requiring p≠0 and p≠∞ prevents a degenerate reciprocal; infinite optimal values remain infinite. No existence of a minimizing coupling is assumed.
Source-present Dirac cost calibration returns the cost evaluated at the pair of atoms.
Source-present Dirac distance calibration returns the ground distance for every nonzero exponent, including∞.

At p=1, both the cost power and the outer root disappear, leaving the primal transport cost for ground edist. This is the W₁ specialization of [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s Definition 6.1, not an assertion of duality with Lipschitz functions. The [Dirac cost formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Cost/Basic.lean#L288) and [Dirac distance formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L487) agree. Joint measurability is enough for the L¹/integral comparison; neither finite moments nor probability normalization are needed when the values are allowed to be infinite.
Source-present Dirac cost calibration returns the cost evaluated at the pair of atoms.
Source-present Dirac distance calibration returns the ground distance for every nonzero exponent, including∞.

In a normed additive group, `‖y-x‖ₑ = edist x y`; reversing the subtraction does not change the norm. Thus the integral of displacement’s pth power is exactly the optimal edist^p cost, hence Wp^p by the [published optimal-value identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L1015). This is [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s normed-space specialization. The statement correctly uses the extended norm and nonnegative integral, allowing infinite values. Measurable opens and second countability justify the measurability used by the bridge.
Published scalar optimal-value identity against which the vector displacement norm is compared.

The displacement function `(x,y)↦y-x` has extended norm equal to ground edist. Its a.e. strong measurability follows from the stated topology and measurable structure, so [the published finite-optimal-cost result](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L1023) transfers exactly to vector-valued `MemLp`. This matches [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s displacement interpretation. The explicit finite-Wp hypothesis is essential; optimality alone may have infinite value. The conclusion needs no completeness of the normed group because it asserts Lp membership, not existence of a vector-valued integral.
Published finite-cost criterion providing actual Lp membership, not just an optimality label.

This is primal attainment for the continuous nonnegative cost d^p, matching [Villani, Theorem 4.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49). A coupling forces equal mass; nonzero finite mass permits normalization to probabilities, and zero mass is handled separately. The published [ground-distance acceptance instance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Existence/Basic.lean#L245) and [power-cost existence theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Existence/Basic.lean#L254) pass. The returned plan attains the Lp infimum, even when that value is ∞. The signature correctly includes Polish/Borel hypotheses and excludes p=0,∞ without claiming finite optimal cost.
Source explicitly marks this as the acceptance instance: ground edist admits an optimal plan on a Polish space.
Published probability-law attainment for the actual power cost; source theorem, not a newly created diagnostic specialization.

An attained zero Lp cost forces x=y almost everywhere under the plan, so its two marginals agree. The converse uses the diagonal plan. This is [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s separation argument, with the Polish/Borel and nonzero finite-exponent assumptions made explicit. The [Dirac calibration](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L487) and [published pseudometric quotient control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Quotient.lean#L58) pass. Only μ is assumed finite: zero Wp supplies a coupling and hence equal finite mass for ν. The theorem claims equality of measures, not uniqueness of optimal plans.
Source-present Dirac distance calibration returns the ground distance for every nonzero exponent, including∞.
Source-present pseudometric control identifies zero Wasserstein distance with equality of separation-quotient pushforwards, including∞.
Source-present pseudometric regression: zero-distance atoms give zero Dirac distance. Their Borel Dirac laws agree; no distinct-law claim.

The infinity endpoint separates laws by reducing to W₁: normalize the common nonzero finite mass, then W₁≤W∞=0 implies equality of the normalized measures, and rescale. Zero mass is handled separately. The [published exponent comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L425) and [endpoint Dirac calibration](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L487) pass. This extends [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s finite-p separation using the actual essential-supremum convention. No finite-p moment or topology characterization is imported at ∞; the [pseudometric quotient control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Quotient.lean#L58) retains the distinction between metric and pseudometric bases.
Probability-normalized exponent comparison justifies the W1≤W∞ step.
Source-present Dirac distance calibration returns the ground distance for every nonzero exponent, including∞.
Source-present pseudometric control identifies zero Wasserstein distance with equality of separation-quotient pushforwards, including∞.

The theorem combines [finite-exponent separation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L1147) with [the separately proved infinity endpoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L1163). Consequently every nonzero exponent is covered, while p=0 is correctly excluded because its measurable objectives vanish. This is [Villani, Chapter 6](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=82)’s separation conclusion with the essential-supremum endpoint added explicitly. The [Dirac calibration](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L487) and [pseudometric regression](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Quotient.lean#L87) pass. The genuine metric hypothesis is retained, and the result does not assert a triangle inequality for 0<p<1.
